toegepas.rede_vinder: Two instances of 'hulle' in one sentence point to different things (the pumpkin leaves, then 'baie blare'); naming the first removes the ambiguity, and the protected wording stays intact.
toegepas.fout: Two instances of 'hulle' in one sentence point to different things: the pumpkin leaves, then 'baie blare'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the pumpkin leaves removes the pronoun clash without adding a fact, and the protected 'Baie blare is plat en breed' stays intact.

toegepas.voor: Dit gee die energie wat die plant vir die werk nodig het en wat gewoonlik van sonlig kom.
toegepas.na: Dit gee die energie wat die plant vir die werk nodig het. Hierdie lig is gewoonlik sonlig.
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written, the light gives energy 'that comes from sunlight', which reads as circular; splitting it says plainly that the light is usually sunlight, and keeps 'gewoonlik'.
toegepas.fout: The light 'gives energy that usually comes from sunlight' reads as circular and stacks two relative clauses.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The split says plainly that the light is usually sunlight, keeps 'gewoonlik' and the energy role, and leaves the protected sentences around it untouched.

toegepas.voor: Hulle bêre dit ook in hulle wortels en blomme, en in hulle vrugte en sade.
toegepas.na: Hulle bêre dit ook in hulle wortels, blomme, vrugte en sade.
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS: no comma before 'en' between parts of one sentence; a single list is also smoother than the repeated 'in hulle'.
toegepas.fout: A comma before 'en' between parts of one sentence, against the AWS 2017, and a clumsy repeated 'in hulle'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: One plain list names the same four parts and reads more smoothly, with nothing added or lost.

toegepas.voor: groei op die stysel in die saad
toegepas.na: gebruik die stysel in die saad om te groei
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'groei op' calques English 'grows on' and can be read as growing on top of the starch.
toegepas.fout: 'groei op die stysel' copies English 'grows on' and can be read as 'opgroei' or as growing on top of the starch.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal says the same thing (the seedling lives on the seed's starch until its leaves open) in natural, unambiguous Afrikaans.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Leaves 'oopvou' is the natural Afrikaans verb for new leaves unfolding.
toegepas.fout: 'oopgaan' is a loose verb for new leaves unfolding.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'oopvou' is the more exact, natural verb for a seedling's first leaves, and the meaning is unchanged.

laat_vaar.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
laat_vaar.voor: kan wel stysel bevat as mense dit bygevoeg het
laat_vaar.na: kan wel stysel bevat wat mense bygevoeg het
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'dit' can be read as the sausage rather than the starch; a relative clause makes clear it is the starch that was added.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'dit' naturally points to the starch, and swapping conditional 'as' for relative 'wat' drops the condition that starch is there only if people added it.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: uit sy kos, en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet
laat_vaar_vorige.na: uit sy kos, en 'n dier wat die plant eet, kry dit ook
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The tacked-on phrase without its own verb reads awkwardly; giving it a verb makes a proper second clause that justifies the comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet' is acceptable Afrikaans, while the proposal is longer and its 'dit' could point to either 'energie' or 'kos'.
